who: William Preston Vaughn, historian at North Texas State University, PhD Ohio State University.

evidence.says: Monte Ross Lewis’s December 1981 history PhD dissertation, Chickasaw Removal, lists William Preston Vaughn as chair and major professor.
The 1972–1973 graduate catalog lists William Preston Vaughn as professor of history, with MA and PhD from Ohio State University.
The authority names William Preston Vaughn and identifies Schools for All and The Antimasonic Party in the United States as his works.

notes: The repository supplies the candidate’s full name for the listed student; institution and doctorate university also agree.

who: Stephen Saunders Webb, early American historian at Syracuse University, PhD Wisconsin–Madison 1965.

evidence.says: Syracuse identifies Stephen Saunders Webb as history professor emeritus, with a Wisconsin–Madison PhD in 1965; his Syracuse appointments began in 1968 and include professor from 1979. Publications include The Governors-General.
The authority identifies Stephen Saunders Webb as the author of The Governors-General.

notes: The full name, publication, doctorate institution and year, and Syracuse career agree with the supervisor record.

who: William Westfall, historian of Canadian religion and culture at York University, PhD University of Toronto.

evidence.says: York identifies William Westfall as faculty since 1977, retired in 2012, and subsequently teaching graduate history; his books concern Protestant institutions and Ontario.
Trinity’s memorial records a doctorate in Canadian history at the University of Toronto followed by teaching history and humanities at York.
Bruce Douville’s The Uncomfortable Pew acknowledgements identify William Westfall as his primary supervisor.
The authority names William Westfall and cites Perspectives on Regions and Regionalism in Canada as a source for the heading.

notes: York affiliation and period, Toronto doctorate, Canadian studies field, and direct confirmation from the listed student support the match.

who: George L. Yaney, historian of Russia at the University of Maryland, PhD Princeton 1961.

evidence.says: Maryland’s 1997–1998 catalog lists George L. Yaney as professor emeritus of history, with a Princeton PhD in 1961.
The 1971 article Professor Yaney Replies identifies its author as George L. Yaney of the University of Maryland.
The authority names George L. Yaney, also using George Yaney, and identifies The Systematization of Russian Government and The Urge to Mobilize as his works.

notes: The institution, name forms, Russian history field, and exact doctorate university and year agree.

who: Jennifer L. Anderson, Atlantic and Caribbean historian at Stony Brook University, PhD New York University 2007.

evidence.says: Stony Brook identifies Jennifer L. Anderson as associate professor with a New York University PhD in 2007 and author of Mahogany: The Costs of Luxury in Early America.
The candidate authority expands J. L. Anderson to Joseph Leslie Anderson and identifies Industrializing the Corn Belt as his work.
The publisher-supplied book record identifies author Joseph Leslie Anderson and says J. L. Anderson teaches US history at Mount Royal College in Calgary.

notes: Candidate p-117851 is Joseph Leslie Anderson, a different historian from Jennifer L. Anderson at Stony Brook.

who: Timothy E. Anna, Latin American historian at the University of Manitoba, PhD Duke 1969.

evidence.says: Manitoba’s archival finding aid records Timothy E. Anna’s Duke PhD in 1969 and appointment to Manitoba’s history department that fall as a Latin America specialist; full professor in 1979 and emeritus in 2010.
The authority identifies Timothy E. Anna as author of Spain and the Loss of America.
The Spanish archives authority identifies Timothy E. Anna as a historian with a Duke history doctorate in 1969 who joined Manitoba that year, with works on Mexican and Spanish American independence.

notes: The full name, exact doctorate university and year, and Manitoba career spanning all listed dissertations agree.

who: Megan C. Armstrong, early modern European historian at McMaster University, PhD Toronto 1998.

evidence.says: McMaster identifies Megan Armstrong as professor of history specializing in early modern Catholicism, with doctoral study at Toronto from 1990 to 1998 and author of The Holy Land and the Early Modern Reinvention of Catholicism.
The publisher identifies Megan C. Armstrong as associate professor of history at McMaster and author of The Politics of Piety (2004).
The authority names Megan C. Armstrong and cites The Politics of Piety (2004) under that name.

notes: The publisher connects the candidate’s fuller name and authority-listed book to McMaster; the Toronto doctorate and field agree.

who: Stephanie D. Bangarth, historian of human rights and migration at King’s/Western, PhD Waterloo (sources give 2003 or 2004).

evidence.says: King’s identifies Stephanie Bangarth as history professor and adjunct teaching professor at Western, at King’s since 2006, with a Waterloo PhD in 2004.
Western’s dissertation list names Stephanie Bangarth as supervisor of Shezan Muhammedi’s Gifts From Amin, matching a listed student and dissertation.

The authority expands Stephanie D. Bangarth to Stephanie Danielle Bangarth and links the name forms Stephanie D. Bangarth and Stephanie Bangarth through The Politics of Rights and Voices Raised in Protest.
The doctoral graduates list places Stephanie D. Bangarth’s The Politics of Rights under 2003 graduates.

notes: Direct dissertation supervision and the authority’s linked name forms confirm the match. King’s gives PhD 2004, as AHA does; Waterloo’s graduate list gives 2003.
